correction_note: schema_version 1 of this file recorded 'NOT_OBSERVED -- minute 10 matched minute 1 in every 3.1 run at draft, small and standard'. That sentence was written by the phase-2 script before the strong-tier v3 runs had landed, and it silently omitted the tier where the effect is largest. The strong tier does NOT hold minute 1 through minute 10. Corrected here with the full per-tier drift so the claim is checkable rather than asserted.
sustained_load_before_throttle: SPLIT BY TIER. draft, small and standard hold flat within +/-3% from minute 1 to minute 10 in all 3 runs and both conditions -- no throttle point exists to record for them. The strong tier decays substantially and consistently: see within_run_drift_percent below.

within_run_drift_percent.method: interval generation rate at minute 10 vs minute 1 of the same 10-minute run, schema_version 3 harness (streamed, wall-clock checkpoints, ignore_eos). One entry per run.

strong_tier_decay.observed: Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE) loses 39-47% of its generation rate between minute 1 and minute 10, in 6 of 6 runs, in both the idle and concurrent conditions. Mistral-Small-24B (dense) loses 5-8% in 5 of 6 runs, with one +5.5% outlier.
strong_tier_decay.consistency: 6/6 runs for the MoE, sign-consistent and tightly clustered. This is not noise and is not a sampling artefact of the v3 harness -- the same harness shows +/-3% at every other tier.
strong_tier_decay.attribution: KV-CACHE GROWTH, not an MoE effect. The percentage figures look MoE-specific; converting them to cost per token of context separates the candidates. At strong a single request spans the whole window (0/1 requests completed, aborted at deadline), so context grows monotonically and each interval's midpoint context is computable from cumulative tokens. MoE: 82.3 -> 135.9 ms/token over +3863 tokens of context = 17.6 us per token of context (runs 13.9/18.2/17.6). Dense: 295.9 -> 316.5 ms/token over +1361 tokens = 14.6 us per token of context (runs 15.1/14.6/-14.2). The two agree within ~20% despite a 3.6x difference in baseline per-token cost, which is what an additive per-context-token attention cost predicts and is not what an MoE expert-working-set effect predicts. The percentage gap is fully accounted for: the MoE reaches 2.8x more context AND has a 3.6x lower baseline, so the same absolute penalty is a much larger fraction. Model checks out against observation: MoE 17.6us x 3863 = +68 ms on 82.3 -> -45% (observed -45%); dense 14.6us x 1361 = +20 ms on 295.9 -> -6.3% (observed -6.5%).
strong_tier_decay.standard_tier_is_not_evidence: The standard 8B is flat at the same -c 8448, but it completes 6 requests per run and resets context every 4096 tokens, so it never tests monotonic growth. Its flatness is a steady state across resets and is neither evidence for nor against.
strong_tier_decay.residual_uncertainty: The two us figures differ by 20%, n=3, and one dense run has the opposite sign. This is CONSISTENT WITH KV growth rather than proof of it. The decisive test is a context sweep at strong (-c 2048 / 4096 / 8448) showing the slope directly. Recorded as attributed-but-unconfirmed.
strong_tier_decay.thermal_ruled_out: NOT RULED OUT formally, but it does not fit: a thermal or power limit would be expected to affect the dense 24B and the standard 8B similarly, and it does not. No die temperature is readable on this board (see acpi_thermal_reason), so this cannot be settled here.
strong_tier_decay.consequence_for_the_router: If the decay is context-driven then the strong tier does not have a single throughput number: a tok/s figure is only meaningful with the context length it was measured at. 6.79 tok/s is the rate at roughly 4.2k tokens of context -- the LAST OBSERVED RATE, NOT A PLATEAU, since the run ended mid-generation with context still growing. Extrapolating the fitted line to a full 8448-token context gives ~4.4 tok/s, which is EXPECTED, not MEASURED, being a two-point linear extrapolation. A router calibrated on the minute-1 sample (~12.4 tok/s) would over-commit by 1.8x; one calibrated on 6.79 for a job longer than ten minutes or one starting from a large prompt would still be optimistic. What the router needs from this tier is a rate as a function of context, not a scalar -- a finding about the SHAPE of capability_profiles.toml, not only its values.

acpi_thermal_reason: MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature unavailable on this board/driver. Common on desktop boards; not a failure of the measurement.
battery_drain_reason: Mains-powered desktop. No battery. Structurally not applicable to this node class, not merely unmeasured.
wall_power_reason: No wall meter available. SPIKE-011 names one as its instrument; until then every power figure in the planning docs is marked EXPECTED, never MEASURED.
noise_reason: No calibrated meter, and a phone-app reading is not a measurement. Recorded as unmeasured rather than estimated.
owner_usable_during_load: DECLARED, not measured -- the 3.4 policy lock treats this node as VESPER-dedicated, so 'usable for the owner during load' is not the condition this node is operated under.
